sections.h2: Where a Bourbon County deed is recorded
sections.html:
The Bourbon County Clerk records deeds in the county building at 301 Main Street, Room 106, in Paris. The same counter serves a Paris townhouse and a horse farm near Millersburg.

Doors open at 8:30 a.m. on weekdays and shut at 4:30 p.m., except Thursday, when the office stays open until 6:00 p.m. Call (859) 987-2142, extension 236. The Property Valuation Administrator is down the hall in Room 15 and the sheriff, who collects tax bills, is in Room 104. For a seller this is convenient: deed, assessment record and tax bill are a few doors apart.

Fire destroyed the Bourbon County courthouse in 1872 and again in 1901, and records went with it. Given that, it pays to review your chain of title before you sign a sales contract. A buyer's title examiner will read the same books at the clerk's counter, and a gap in an old legal description can delay the closing.

  • Farm parcels can carry several tax parcels, and each extra reference adds $4.00 on the clerk's schedule.
  • Easements, leases and plats are recorded documents too, and each has its own line on the fee schedule.
  • The title search happens before closing, so recording problems tend to surface early.

A deed costs $50 and a deed of correction $46 on the posted schedule, which is dated January 1, 2020. A note on it says fees may vary slightly, so phone the office for today's total before mailing anything.

Selected recording fees
DocumentFee
Deed$50.00
Deed of correction$46.00
Mortgage$80.00
Mortgage with MERS or assignment$126.00
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46.00
Affidavit of descent$50.00
Power of attorney$50.00
Will$47.00
Lis pendens notice$46.00

Page count changes the total. Past page five, most documents cost $3.00 more per page, and each added parcel reference is $4.00. A farm deed with several parcels costs more than a short town lot deed.

The seller owes a transfer tax equal to $1 for every $1,000 of price, with rounding up in $500 steps. Payment is made at the counter, and the clerk won't accept the deed until it is made. The base is the value written in the deed, which on a sale includes loan balances secured against the property.

Some transfers owe no tax at all. The common ones:

  • Foreclosure transfers, or a property handed to the lender in place of foreclosure.
  • Spouse-to-spouse moves, ex-spouses in a divorce included.
  • A parent giving to a child, or a grandparent to a grandchild, for token money.
  • Corrective deeds that repair an earlier recording.

Kentucky lists items a deed must carry, and the clerk can't file one that omits them. Its face must name the seller and the buyer, give a mailing address for each, and state what was paid. One more item is required: an address for the tax bill in the year of transfer.

On a sale, both sides or their agents sign a notarized, sworn statement that the stated price is the entire price. A gift calls for a statement saying so, plus an estimated fair cash value. The deed also has to show where the seller's ownership came from, by citing the earlier deed's book and page or by explaining an inheritance. Most sellers leave the drafting to the title company or a Kentucky attorney.

sections.h2: Selling a house that came through an estate
sections.html:
Before an estate is closed, the executor or administrator files a sworn list with the clerk showing who receives each property and what it is worth. The affidavit of descent is priced at $50 on the clerk's schedule.

This step often decides whether an inherited Paris house can sell quickly. A buyer's title company wants the chain from the deceased owner to the heirs in the Bourbon County records before it will insure a purchase. If the estate hasn't filed, start there, and ask the clerk's office which documents your situation needs.

1. Dig out your own deed and note the book and page, since the new deed has to cite it.
  2. Ask the title company who is drafting the deed, and make sure the tax-bill address for the buyer is on it.
  3. Find out whether the sale price will be stated in full. The sworn statement from both sides has to match the deed.
  4. Call the clerk's office at (859) 987-2142, extension 236, for a current fee total before the closing agent sends payment.
  5. If a lien or an open estate affects the property, deal with it before the closing date, not on it.

The clerk holds the deed until the transfer tax and the recording fee are paid, so those two amounts are the last thing between a signed deed and a recorded one.

The clerk records several kinds of claims, and any of them can turn up in a title search: mechanics liens, judgment liens, lis pendens notices, tax liens and child support liens.

  • A judgment lien needs the court, case number and amount, and the creditor or attorney signs it.
  • A lis pendens warns that title is in litigation and must name the court and action number.
  • A mechanics lien needs a notarized statement of the amount due and a property description specific enough to identify the parcel.
  • Each lien has its own release document, which is also recorded for a fee.

If you know of a lien, get a payoff letter from the holder and ask for a release you can record, so the closing agent can settle it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Other Bourbon County offices a seller may need
sections.html:
They sit close together. The PVA is in Room 15, the sheriff in Room 104 and the treasurer in Room 210 of 301 Main Street, all on the same weekday schedule. Planning and code enforcement, which handle permits, zoning approvals and ordinance complaints, are at 525 High Street, and their number is (859) 987-2150.

A seller with an unpermitted porch or a code complaint on a Paris rental should call that High Street office before listing, since an open violation can surface during a buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: Bourbon County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Bourbon County had an estimated 20,243 residents in 2025 and about 9,399 housing units. Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $229,300, owners live in 63.7% of homes, the typical monthly rent is $822 and the typical household takes in $61,354. Paris is the seat, with Millersburg and North Middletown the other towns, and the county is mostly rolling farmland in the Lexington area.

A house with a tenant, a repair list or a stalled estate records the same way as any other. The deed, the transfer tax and any releases are the parts a seller controls.

faqs.q: Where is the Bourbon County Clerk's office?
faqs.a: At 301 Main Street, Room 106, in Paris, Kentucky. Weekday hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a 6:00 p.m. close on Thursday.

faqs.q: How much does the clerk charge to record a deed in Bourbon County?
faqs.a: The posted schedule lists $50 for a deed and $46 for a deed of correction, with $3 for each page past five. That schedule is dated January 1, 2020, so confirm the current amount with the office.

faqs.q: Who pays the Kentucky transfer tax on a Bourbon County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. The clerk collects it at the counter and won't record the deed until it is paid.

faqs.q: Does a deed in lieu of foreclosure owe the transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. Kentucky exempts a transfer made in a foreclosure proceeding or by a voluntary surrender in lieu of foreclosure. The mortgage holder must file that deed within 45 days after it is signed.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Bourbon County if the property is in another county?
faqs.a: No. Recording happens in the county that holds the land, so this clerk can't file a deed for a parcel in a neighboring county.
